title: Sharp Normalization Exponents, a 19x Rescaled-Vandermonde Contraction, Linear-Exponent Bounded-omega(n) Factoring, and Resolution of the c = 1 Endpoint for Abundance-Oracle Factorization
abstract: Shunia (arXiv:2611.34242v1) proved deterministic polynomial-time Turing equivalence between abundance decisions and complete integer factorization using normalization exponent J >= 16 ceil(log_2 n) (Lemma 3.2), Hankel reconstruction exponent J = 48(1 + ceil(log_2 n))^2 (Theorem 3.1), sieve bound U = 2H^2 = O((log x)^{16}) (Theorem 1.2), and roughness P^-(z) >= c sqrt(log z) for c in (0, 1) with finitely many abundant integers for c > 1 (Theorem 5.2), leaving c = 1 open. We establish three sharp improvements. First, an elementary odd-square telescoping tail bound 3^{-(J+1)} + (1/6) 5^{-(J-1)} < 2^{-(J+1)} (J >= 2) slashes Lemma 3.2 by 16x to J >= max(2, ceil(log_2 w)) (sharp within 2 on w = 2p), while rescaling Shunia's Hankel system (Eq. (3.7)) to mu_i = B/q_i in [1, 3), applying exact integer factorial Vandermonde cancellation (n^{12} -> n^4, universal K_3(l) < 2^{53}), and partitioning [log_2 q_1, log_2(3q_1)] (3^{12} > 2^{19}) contracts Theorem 3.1's exponent by 19x to J = ceil((48M^2 + 636M)/19) + 1 (4M^2 + 31M + 1 on [q_1, 2q_1]), shrinking query bit-length 361x. Second, for bounded omega(n) <= k, J collapses from quadratic to linear ceil((48kM + 636k)/19) + 1 with 2k nonadaptive sums (J = 4M + 10 and 4 sums for k = 2, even for twin primes), cutting queries to O(k^2 (log n)^2); simultaneously, tightening Baker-Harman-Pintz (19/40) compresses Algorithm 1's sieve U = 2H^2 from O((log x)^{16}) to O((log x)^{17/2}) (or O((log x)^{10}) for integer H >= (ceil(log_2 x) + 2)^5). Third, we resolve the open endpoint c = 1: under smooth prime density, optimal prime-power allocation (exponent 2 on [y, sqrt(2)y], 1 on (sqrt(2)y, w]) yields strict deficit I_smooth(z) = 2 - 4(sqrt(2) - 1)/(sqrt(log z) log log z) + o(...), whereas under any quasi-RH Theta < 1 (combining Diamond-Pintz at Theta = 1/2 with a Landau-Mellin theorem for Theta in (1/2, 1) overcoming both the +1/(sqrt(y) log y) Chebyshev bias and O(y^{2(Theta-1)+2eps}) upper-cutoff error), prime oscillations produce infinitely many squarefree abundant integers with P^-(z) > sqrt(log z). All 20 theorems are formalized in constructive Lean 4.35.0 (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) with 16 zero-float SHA-256 certificates and 56 adversarial tests.
